$comment: ★★ A C FILE WHOSE LAST LINE IS A `//` COMMENT WITH NO NEWLINE COMPILES AND RUNS (P68 round 8, D-C-LINE-COMMENT-AT-END-OF-FILE-REFUSED). The last line of `main.c` is `#define LAST_LINE 1 // …` and no newline follows it, so at the end of input TWO frames are open: the directive's (a `popAtNewline` mode, `closes` by construction) and the comment's. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c17`, and `-std=c2x -pedantic -Wall -Wextra`), aarch64 gcc, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51 (`/std:c17`, `/std:clatest`, `/W4`) all accept this shape, a bare last-line `// c`, and `// c \\` with no newline; clang warns only under `-pedantic` (`-Wnewline-eof`). DSS refused all three with `P_UnterminatedComment: EOF inside lexer mode 'line-comment'`. ★ THE FIX IS A DECLARATION: `c.lang.json`'s `line-comment` mode declares `atEndOfInput: closes`. C does NOT declare the gas dialects' `endOfInputImplies`, because the preprocessor re-lexes token-paste products and `#if` scratch text through the same tokenizer and an implied newline at the end of each would be a line boundary nobody wrote. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: remove `atEndOfInput` from the `line-comment` mode and this example is refused again with `P_UnterminatedComment`. `block-comment` keeps the default, because every reference refuses a `/*` the file never closes. ⚠ `.gitattributes` pins `examples/**` to LF, which never adds a final newline, so the shape survives every checkout.
